newsitem.title: GABON: Teachers strike blocks start of Gabon schools.
newsitem.headline: Teachers strike blocks start of Gabon schools.

text.p: A strike by primary and secondary school teachers in Gabon prevented the start of the school year on Tuesday, as teachers across the country obeyed a union call to boycott classes, witnesses said.
The teachers are demanding various bonuses, a housing allowance and the granting of equal rights for teachers in religious-based schools.

Christiane Bitoughat, general secretary of the National Education Teachers Union (SEENA), which represents most teachers in the Central African oil-producing nation, said the authorities had not satisfied the union's demands.
The union issued the strike call on Friday.
The junior education minister said on state television on Monday that the teachers' action threatened to compromise the future of Gabon's children and could lead to a lost year.

The World Bank and International Monetary Fund have been encouraging African states to widen primary education, arguing that by increasing the number of people who can read, write and do simple maths they will help their economies grow.
